overview: This Senate resolution names August 21, 2026, Fentanyl Prevention and Awareness Day. Fentanyl is a synthetic opioid, a powerful painkiller-type drug about 100 times stronger than morphine, and illegally made fentanyl is often mixed into other drugs or pressed into fake pills that look like real medicine, so many people take it without knowing. The resolution notes that synthetic opioids caused nearly two-thirds of U.S. drug overdose deaths in 2025 and honors people who have died and the families working to warn others. It encourages Americans to educate young people about the dangers, to choose drug-free lives, and to take part in drug prevention activities. It does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it on August 7, 2026.
for: Supporters say a national day of awareness helps families and schools warn young people that any pill bought outside a pharmacy could contain a deadly dose of fentanyl.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, and that awareness days alone do little without added funding for treatment and prevention.
